forces.title: Digital advertising and streaming are key future growth arenas
forces.description: The report identifies "Digital advertisements" and "Streaming video" as two of 18 potential future "arenas" of competition expected to display exceptional growth and competitive dynamism over the next 15 years. These arenas reshape value creation by introducing new competitors, generating demand shocks across value chains, and concentrating demand on critical inputs or technologies. This signifies a long-term structural shift in economic growth drivers, with significant implications for Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IG0903).
forces.source_title: Strategy in the age of arenas

forces.title: Streaming platforms reshape media profit pools by controlling customer relationships
forces.description: The rise of streaming platforms is structurally altering the media landscape by taking control of customer relationships, shifting profit pools from traditional media players to these platforms. This highlights how arenas like streaming can gradually shift industry profit pools and who captures them. This development is a key structural change impacting IN090301 (Search, Social & Content Platforms), as ad-driven video/content sharing platforms thrive by aggregating user attention and controlling direct customer access, leading to a redistribution of value within the broader media ecosystem.
forces.source_title: Strategy in the age of arenas

forces.title: Application-layer AI valuations are correcting, shifting M&A focus
forces.description: In the Technology, Media, and Telecommunications sector, a bifurcation dynamic is observed where infrastructure-layer assets (data centers, computing, power) command extraordinary valuations, while application-layer companies are experiencing valuation corrections. This shift means M&A activity in the second half of 2026 is likely to move towards the application layer due to more attractive entry valuations and easier quantification of synergies. For IN090301 and IN090302 (application-layer), this represents a cyclical adjustment in investor perception and M&A focus.
forces.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

forces.title: M&A focus shifting to application layer due to attractive valuations
forces.description: Following valuation corrections in application-layer companies within the Technology, Media, and Telecommunications sector, M&A activity is projected to shift towards these assets in the second half of 2026. This is driven by more attractive entry valuations and the potential for easier quantification of synergies compared to infrastructure assets. For Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IN090301, IN090302), this creates an upside driver for deal activity, allowing strategic and financial buyers to acquire differentiated capabilities, provided rigorous due diligence is applied.
forces.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

forces.title: Power availability constraints pose binding risk for AI-driven growth
forces.description: The energy and utilities sector is witnessing a decisive shift where power availability has become a binding constraint on AI-driven growth. This means that securing sufficient power is reshaping M&A activity in the energy sector, as hyperscalers move to own generating capacity for data center demand. For Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IG0903), particularly those relying on data centers for AI operations or large-scale content delivery, this represents a key risk as power scarcity could impact operational scalability, costs, and ultimately growth trajectories.
forces.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

forces.title: AI fostering new content formats on open platforms like YouTube
forces.description: AI's impact on film and TV production extends beyond traditional workflows, fundamentally reshaping the industry. Similar to how the internet enabled open platforms like YouTube and new short-form content, AI is expected to unlock entirely new content types, formats, and distribution models. This represents a structural change for IN090301 (Search, Social & Content Platforms), as ad-driven video/content sharing platforms are poised to benefit from increased content diversity and potentially new monetization avenues driven by AI-enabled creation.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: Proliferation of low-quality AI-generated content on platforms
forces.description: The emergence of AI tools is leading to an enormous volume of low-quality, AI-generated video ("AI slop") on platforms like YouTube and TikTok. Despite platforms' efforts to control it, this content is expected to continue exploding. For IN090301 (Search, Social & Content Platforms), this represents a key risk as it could dilute content quality, potentially diminish user experience, and challenge the platforms' ability to maintain engagement and advertiser appeal. Managing and filtering this volume will be crucial for these platforms.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: AI democratizes content creation, fostering grassroots creators and diverse content
forces.description: AI tools, accessible via low-cost subscriptions, are democratizing content creation by enabling anyone to experiment and create high-quality content. This fundamentally differs from past technological disruptions that required enormous upfront investment. For IN090301 (Search, Social & Content Platforms), this is an upside driver, as it facilitates a "long tail" of grassroots creators producing higher-quality content, alongside top-end premium storytelling. This increased volume and diversity of content can enhance user engagement and attract broader audiences to ad-driven platforms.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: End-user and creative community rejection of AI-generated content
forces.description: Industry leaders are concerned about end-user acceptance of AI-generated content, as historical patterns show initial user rejection of new technologies, which currently is prevalent for AI-generated media. Additionally, there is a risk of rejection from creative communities, evidenced by labor union strikes (SAG-AFTRA, Writers Guild) and debates around AI dubbing and digital likeness rights. These factors pose key risks for IN090301, as content platforms rely heavily on both audience engagement and creative talent contributions, and widespread rejection could hinder adoption and growth.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: IP infringement and hallucination/bias risks in AI content generation
forces.description: The use of AI in content creation introduces significant risks related to intellectual property (IP) and rights infringement, as many AI models are trained on internet content, some of which is copyright protected. Furthermore, concerns exist regarding "hallucination and bias" in AI models, particularly in casting, marketing, and script development, which could lead to inaccurate representation or skewed opinions. These are critical risks for IN090301, as platforms hosting AI-generated content could face legal challenges and reputational damage if such issues are not adequately addressed and managed.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: Advertiser reliance on "black box optimization" systems for AI media strategy
forces.description: As attention, decision-making, buying, conversion, and measurement consolidate within integrated AI environments, advertisers face increased dependence on platform-provided data and "black box optimization" systems. 42% of surveyed advertisers identify this as a key risk to their media investment strategy. For IN090302 (Digital Advertising & Ad Tech) and IN090301 (platforms hosting these ads), this poses a challenge to transparency and control, as advertisers may lose visibility over ad placements and performance within single platforms, hindering effective strategy and measurement.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Advertising spend shifts to AI-native platforms and direct buying
forces.description: Advertising economics are redistributing, with over 50% of advertisers investing in ads embedded in AI-generated answers. Notably, 40% of AI-driven spend is reallocating from traditional search and the open web towards platforms with superior data, measurement, and transaction capabilities. This reinforces a decade-long trend of direct ad buying, which has nearly tripled since 2019. For IN090301 and IN090302, this represents a structural change, benefiting integrated AI-native platforms and walled gardens that offer automated targeting and closed-loop measurement, while creating headwinds for traditional ad tech and open web publishers.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI-native buying agents compress traditional ad tech intermediation
forces.description: The ad tech "middle" is compressing due to AI-native buying agents, which can replicate cross-platform optimization within a single workflow. This development threatens to eliminate key use cases for supply-side platforms (SSPs), ad exchanges, traditional demand-side platforms (DSPs), and undifferentiated middleware. With 82% of surveyed advertisers planning to buy AI ad formats directly in the next 12 months, intermediation layers built on cross-platform arbitrage are facing a diminished role. This is a significant headwind for IN090302, driving consolidation and requiring adaptation towards specialized infrastructure or neutral measurement services.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Ad tech to pivot to neutral cross-platform identity, measurement, and AI audit services
forces.description: As the ad tech middle compresses due to AI-native buying agents, the opportunity for ad tech firms lies in serving as connective tissue across walled gardens and AI platforms. This involves focusing on neutral, cross-platform identity and measurement solutions to enable advertisers to compare performance and manage spend across diverse environments. Additionally, trust and governance become differentiators, allowing ad tech firms to offer independent AI performance audits, validation services, and testing platforms. This pivot creates new opportunities for IN090302 to provide essential infrastructure rather than intermediation.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI accelerates eroding open web economics and traditional search traffic decline
forces.description: AI is accelerating the decline of traditional search traffic and the eroding economics of the open web, as consumers become increasingly comfortable with AI-generated answers. This trend makes click-driven, scale-dependent publishing unviable and significantly exposes long-tail, SEO-dependent sites without user subscription models. While not directly IN090301 (which focuses on platforms aggregating attention) or IN090302 (pure-play ad tech), this impacts their ecosystem, particularly ad tech companies that rely on open-web inventory and search engines' traditional ad placements.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Walled gardens expand into commerce, integrating AI agents for monetization
forces.description: Established "walled gardens" are well-positioned for the new advertising era, actively expanding beyond attention monetization into commerce and agent offerings. Examples include TikTok's projected $30 billion in commerce GMV by 2028, YouTube prioritizing commerce, and Meta integrating AI agents across its apps. This strategic shift represents a significant tailwind for IN090301 (Search, Social & Content Platforms), as these platforms leverage their user base and data to create new, integrated revenue streams from direct commerce transactions and enhanced advertising models.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI-native platforms developing advertising models for conversational interfaces
forces.description: A new category of AI-native platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) is gaining traction for product research, leveraging conversational AI interfaces and agent layers for faster, more useful recommendations. These platforms have privileged access to decision moments and behavioral data but lack mature advertising models. This presents a significant new opportunity for IN090302 (Digital Advertising & Ad Tech) to develop novel monetization strategies like sponsored answers, agent-readable claims, affiliate commerce, and bidding into recommendations. The outcome will determine their role: whether they build new walled gardens, partner, or remain neutral interfaces.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Retail sector reduces advertising and marketing spend amid caution
forces.description: The UK retail sector is experiencing fragile sales, volatile trading, and national budget uncertainty, leading businesses to reduce spending, particularly in advertising and marketing. Retailers are adopting a "wait and see" stance on capex, with financial distress remaining frequent. This overall caution and reduction in ad spending presents a cyclical headwind for IN090302 (Digital Advertising & Ad Tech), as retailers are key clients. The decreased demand for advertising services could impact revenue and growth for ad tech providers.

forces.title: Chip supply disruption due to AI data center demand threatens production
forces.description: The Computers & Telecoms sector faces a risk of chip supply disruption in 2026 due to the absorption of global demand from AI data center projects. This threatens to impact production and prices, although a gradual usage of AI technology in consumer and corporate segments may not justify a very large increase in hardware prices. For Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IG0903), which heavily relies on computing infrastructure for its operations, this represents a key risk, as chip shortages could lead to higher operational costs, constrained expansion, and potential service disruptions.

viewpoints.title: AI-driven valuations in technology, media, and telecom create market paradox
viewpoints.description: Despite leading first-half deal value, the Technology, Media, and Telecommunications sector (which includes Internet Platforms & Digital Media) recorded the lowest M&A sentiment at 52. Buyers are investing rapidly in AI themes but harbor caution regarding the sustainability of AI-driven valuations. This paradox suggests a market where capital is committed at pace, but underlying confidence is low, particularly in business models with high exposure to AI disruption like Software as a Service, creating uncertainty for valuations within the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

viewpoints.title: Ad-driven content distributors well-positioned to benefit from AI-led content boom
viewpoints.description: Jamie Vickers, Partner at McKinsey, states that distributors of content, especially ad-driven platforms like YouTube (classified under Search, Social & Content Platforms), are well-positioned to gain significantly from the AI transformation in media. These platforms act as "choke points" for content release and will benefit from the expected increase in content choices and potentially better pricing for consumers. This positions ad-driven content platforms favorably to capture value as AI fosters greater content production and diverse formats.
viewpoints.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

viewpoints.title: AI-driven discovery and recommendations consolidating attention in walled gardens
viewpoints.description: AI is profoundly reshaping media and advertising by consolidating consumer attention and traffic into AI-driven environments, particularly within "walled gardens" such as social media platforms. Over 50% of Instagram content and over 95% of TikTok watch time already come from algorithmic feeds. Meta reported a 5% increase in Facebook time spent (Q3 2025) and over 30% increase in Instagram Reels watch time (US, YoY) due to AI-driven recommendations. This signals a positive shift for Search, Social & Content Platforms, as brand visibility increasingly depends on these powerful AI systems.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

new_opportunities.opportunity: New use cases for AI shopping agents

Forecasts suggest 20-50% of traffic from traditional open-web search could be at risk by 2030 due to consumer discovery moving into AI environments. demand_drivers.description: A growing share of consumers use AI tools to mediate purchasing, from product research to transaction completion.

Walled gardens like TikTok, YouTube, and Meta are prioritizing commerce as a new revenue stream beyond traditional advertising.

new_opportunities.opportunity: Commerce and agent offerings within established walled gardens

This figure highlights the increasing monetization potential for ad-driven content platforms (IN090301) as they expand beyond traditional attention monetization into integrated commerce and agent offerings.
market_sizing.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

demand_drivers.description: PC and console gaming, with only 4% ad revenue share, represent a significant opportunity compared to mobile gaming's 48%.

pnl_drivers.description: Gaming studios can expand beyond consumer-paid models to capture additional revenue from advertising, improving ARPU.
